descriptionChirho: Describes a male or group of males who have not undergone physical circumcision, typically used of the Philistines and other non-Israelite peoples as a term of reproach.
Used in construct state ('uncircumcised of heart/lips/ears') to describe spiritual dullness, moral obstinacy, or inability to function properly, extending the circumcision metaphor to inner organs.
Applied to fruit trees in their first three years (Lev 19:23), treating their produce as impure or off-limits, analogous to an uncircumcised foreskin that must be removed before consecration.
